name: Lily Bay State Park
note: Recommended by Grok as one of the best campgrounds in Maine. Some campsites are lakefront. --AWH  Waterfront-audited 2026-06-18: lakefront confirmed via Rowell Cove outer drive-in sites (kayak-launch from site); note many premier waterfront sites are walk-in tent (peninsula 33-38). Two loops (Dunn Point, Rowell Cove), no hookups; book waterfront sites early via CampWithMe. --Claude

name: Sebago Lake State Park
note: Recommended by Grok as one of the best campgrounds in Maine.  Some campsites appear to be lakefront.  --AWH  Waterfront-audited 2026-06-18: downgraded to not waterfront - the Sebago shore is day-use beaches (Witch Cove, Naples Beach) and the 250 sites are set back in pine forest behind them; no campsite frontage, lake views pine-screened. Big sandy beaches for day use; 92 sites have E/W hookups. Pin moved onto the camping loops. --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends (reservations made before July 1), 4 (reservations made during February)

name: Meriwether Lewis Campground
note: Natchez Trace Parkway campground in a wooded loop; sites are first-come-first-served.  --AWH

name: Tobyhanna State Park
note: Some sites from 91-131 may have partial lake view, of which CampsitePhotos recommends 101, 111, 113, 115, 117, and 119 --Claude  Tobyhanna Lake is to be drawn down from spring 2027 to December 31, 2028 for dam and dredging work; the lake, boat launches and swimming area close to the public then, while the modern campground stays open (ReserveAmerica alert, read 2026-10-20). --Claude

name: Green Ridge State Forest Headquarters
note: Designated primitive campsites scattered through the forest on ridges and hollows; many sit near the Potomac River, Fifteen Mile Creek and other stream corridors. As of October 2026 DNR warns that 'Some roads and campsites may be temporarily closed following a recent flood event. Contact headquarters for current conditions.' --Claude  Use caution: DNR says the roads to the campsites are gravel or dirt and 'Four-wheel drive may be required depending on conditions' (kept per AWH 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Gary's Family Campground
note: Non-waterfront sites in the woods, high up in the hills.  Nice view from lodge area.  --AWH  CLOSED as a campground (checked 2026-10-15): the property was sold and is now GORA (gorastay.com), five rental cabins with no RV or tent sites. Kept because trip 71 stayed here. --Claude

name: Hopkins Prairie Campground
note: Hopkins Prairie is a seasonal prairie/marsh in Ocala National Forest; sites are in the surrounding forest and not on a permanent water body. Run by the concessionaire Naventure; reached by unmarked, unimproved forest roads, and low tree branches over the campground road may limit vehicle height (USFS, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Mike Roess Gold Head Branch State Park
note: Campground sites are in a wooded area; the park's lakes are in ravines/sinkholes and sites are not directly on them. The Turkey Oak loop has been closed for renovations since March 2026, and the Little Lake Johnson swimming area since July 6, 2026 (low water) (park page, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: River Junction Campground (Withlacoochee State Forest)
note: Campground is reported to be quiet and peaceful with a nice sandy beach on the Withalacochee River; campsites are not waterfront.  --AWH River Junction Boat Ramp closed since June 6, 2026 for repairs and low water (FDACS, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Skidaway Island State Park
note:
Recommended in _Where_Should_We_Camp_Next?_ by Stephanie Puglisi
RVLife 9.2/10
Campground is set in a maritime forest interior; the marsh and Skidaway Narrows are accessed via trails.  --AWH
A partial campground renovation began February 2, 2026 and is scheduled to last one year (park page, read 2026-10-30). --Claude

name: Letchworth State Park Campground
note:
Recommended in _Where_Should_We_Camp_Next?_ by Stephanie Puglisi
Campground is on the plateau above the Genesee River gorge; the park is famous for waterfalls but the campground is not on the river. --Claude
Five new shower buildings are being built: from summer 2026 through spring 2027 loops 100 and 200 stay open and the other loops close in phases (ReserveAmerica, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: North Creek Campground
note: Small first-come-first-served USFS campground in the George Washington National Forest with sites positioned directly along North Creek. --AWH  FCFS only - pay on-site (kiosk/Scan & Pay), not bookable in advance. --Claude

name: Walnut Flats Campground
note: Small no-fee first-come-first-served USFS campground near the Appalachian Trail.  --AWH  Shaded sites clustered around a grassy opening; Dismal Creek (stocked trout) and the Falls of Dismal nearby. --Claude

name: North Rim Campground
note: Perched on the quieter, less-visited North Rim at high elevation, this campground provides jaw-dropping vistas of the Grand Canyon's vast expanse. The elevation and remoteness enhance the sweeping views of the canyon's layered cliffs. --Claude Temporarily closed post-Dragon Bravo Fire (2025); North Rim reopened May 15, 2026, campground expected to reopen June 2026 - no water/RV hookups, Stage 2 fire restrictions. --Claude Rechecked 2026-09-30: campground reopened June 1, 2026 (recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Lakeside State Park
note:
Despite the name, the campground is set back from Lake Ontario in wooded loops.  --AWH
Many ash trees in the campground were cut because of emerald ash borer, leaving a more open canopy (ReserveAmerica alert, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Jonathan Dickinson State Park River Campground
note: Park on the Loxahatchee River with two campgrounds, a nature boardwalk, observation tower, and kayaking options.  Campgrounds are not waterfront.  --AWH  Reserve Florida marks 17 or more River Campground sites 'This site floods in moderate to heavy rains' (read 2026-10-21). Since Oct. 2025 the River Campground's south bathhouses have been closed for renovation; the south family/ADA bathroom with shower and the north bathhouse are open (park page, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Hidden Valley Campground
note: Small first-come-first-served USFS campground near Warm Springs, Lake Sherwood, and Lake Moomaw. --AWH  FCFS - pay on-site only, not bookable in advance. --Claude

name: Blowing Springs Campground
note: Small USFS campground near Warm Springs with a unique geological feature that creates a duct that blows air out of the rocks at a constant 58 degrees. --AWH  FCFS only - pay on-site (Scan & Pay), not bookable in advance. --Claude

name: McClintic Point Primitive Campground
note: Small first-come-first-served campground on Lake Moomaw near Bolar Mountain Recreation Area.  All sites claim to accommodate 21 feet RVs but will probably handle a few feet more.  A couple sites appear to be waterfront.  Route 603 NW of the campground is a narrow one-lane gravel road with steep drop-offs not suitable for RVs.  Campground should be accessed from route 600 instead.  --AWH

name: Little Fort Campground
note: Small minimally-maintained campground near Woodstock Tower; first-come-first-served, only a few RV sites. --AWH

name: Holland State Park
note: Campground on Lake Michigan with sites behind the dunes in what looks like a large paved parking lot.  --AWH Lake Macatawa campground's Woodstock loop (sites 117-211) is closed for most of the 2027 season while a new toilet and shower building goes in; sites 1-116 stay open (DNR park page, read 2026-10-22). --Claude

name: Todd Lake Recreation Area Campground
note: There is a small lake nearby, but the campground is not on the lake. --AWH  FCFS - pay on-site (Scan & Pay), not bookable online. USFS notes "not suitable for large RVs" (18 moderate sites) - a 23-ft rig fits some but options are limited. --Claude

name: North River Campground
note: Small pleasant-looking Forest Service campground on the North River (which is really just a creek, and some say it can be dry by the end of the summer). Seven of the nine sites are right on the creek. First come first served, and reportedly fills up on summer weekends. --AWH  FCFS - not on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Wolf Gap Recreation Area
note:
Small campground on the VA/WV border.  First-come-first-served.  Close to trailheads for Big Schloss and Tibbet Knob.  --AWH
Since July 2025 recreation.gov lists a Scan & Pay fee, paid on site. --Claude

name: Elizabeth Furnace Family Campground
note: Campground is located alongside a creek. Some sites are directly adjacent to the creek. --AWH  Family campground is FCFS - pay on-site (Scan & Pay / Iron Ranger), not reservable online; only the separate Group Camp is reservable. --Claude

name: Dolly Sods boondocking sites #3
note: High-elevation dispersed sites near Dolly Sods Wilderness.  --AWH  AWH 2026-10-21 (driven past): each has an unpaved driveway leading to a clearing away from the road, which matters because Forest Order 21-94 bars camping within 300 ft of FR 19/75. --Claude

name: Dolly Sods boondocking sites #2
note: Dolly Sods high-elevation plateau; not waterfront. --AWH  AWH 2026-10-21 (driven past): each has an unpaved driveway leading to a clearing away from the road, which matters because Forest Order 21-94 bars camping within 300 ft of FR 19/75. --Claude

name: Dolly Sods boondocking sites #1
note: Several roadside wooded sites near Dolly Sods wilderness area.  --AWH  AWH 2026-10-21 (driven past): each has an unpaved driveway leading to a clearing away from the road, which matters because Forest Order 21-94 bars camping within 300 ft of FR 19/75. --Claude

name: Grindstone Campground
note: High-elevation mountain campground; not waterfront. --AWH  USFS campground in the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area (George Washington and Jefferson National Forests), at 3,800 ft in the Fairwood Valley; standard electric sites have 30-amp service and water. Closed for the 2026 season (USFS alert, July 8, 2026) to replace aging infrastructure and repair Hurricane Helene damage; no reopening date announced, so verify before relying on it. --Claude

name: Flag Rock Campground
note: High-elevation campground operated by City of Norton; first-come-first-served; fresh water and dump station; closed winters. --AWH

name: Christopher Run Campground
note: 7.5/8.5★/9  Note that the campground's "lakefront" sites are on the beach, and the beach is open to anyone who is staying at the campground. --AWH  [RV Life: 4★, price $$$ (3/4). --Claude]  Reserve by phone/email request form (540-894-4744, deposit required) --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends (Memorial Day - Labor Day), 3 on holidays

name: San Carlos RV Park & Islands - Fort Myers
note:
Waterfront RV park in the Fort Myers Beach area with sites directly on San Carlos Bay.  --AWH  Two pets per site.  From December to April, boat, utility and car trailers must be stored off the property, and each site gets one vehicle.  Free Wi-Fi; electric is metered on monthly sites.  Check-in is at noon, check-out at 11 a.m. --Claude
MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights April-October, by the month only January-March, 3 nights on holidays (sancarlosrv.com contact page, read 2026-10-20). --Claude

Booking: min stay 28 nights (January to March, by the month only), 3 on holidays (Memorial Day, July 4 and Labor Day), 2 (April to October)

name: Gamble Rogers
note: About half the sites in the beachside loop are oceanfront, but dunes and vegetation may block the view. --AWH  BEACHSIDE CLOSED: 'Effective June 23, 2026: The beachside campground, day use parking lot and restroom ... are currently closed for an improvement project' (park page, read 2026-10-21; no reopening date given; Reserve Florida showed no beachside site free in December 2026). The Riverside campground is open. RVers should use I-95 exit 284 or 268, not 278 (tight turns, low tree clearance). --Claude

name: Hillsborough River State Park
note:
The river runs through the park but the campground is a standard loop set back in the woods; sites are not directly on the riverbank. --AWH
New bathhouse being built in Loop 1 from Oct. 16, 2026, with construction equipment moving through the campground (park alert, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Spruce Run Recreation Area
note: Campground on Spruce Run Reservoir with several lakefront RV sites. Lakefront sites are clearly marked with blue icons on the reservation system map. --AWH Reservable online via NJ Outdoors. --Claude Two-night minimum on every campsite booking, weeknights included (NJ state regulation; 2026-10-10); kept as an exception to the no-standing-minimum rule per AWH. --Claude

name: Pohick Bay Regional Park
note: From site 37 you can see the Potomac River through the trees in the wintertime. --AWH  MINIMUM STAY (NOVA Parks 2026 campground rules, read 2026-10-20): electric-only sites 2 nights April-October, water/electric sites 2 nights all year, full-hookup sites 3 nights April-October (7 when booked more than 60 days out); 3 nights on holiday weekends; one night only on electric-only sites November-March. --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights in summer (April 1 - October 31), 3 on holidays

name: First Landing State Park Campground
note: Numerous beachfront sites, but vegetation and dunes may block water view. --AWH A 23-ft motorhome fits the 27 EW-30ft sites; the 36 EW-50ft sites are for RVs 32-50 ft only and the 45 EW-20ft sites take rigs only to 20 ft (DCR, read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Grouseland Hospitality
note: Several campsites on a mountain ridge with nice views of the surrounding countryside.  --AWH  Two-night minimum on every site (Hipcamp, 2026-10-10); kept as an exception to the no-standing-minimum rule per AWH. --Claude

name: River Forks Park & Campground
note: Locally managed campground on a peninsula in Lake Lanier.  Many of sites are directly on the water.  --AWH  Hall County (local government) park on Lake Lanier at 3500 Keith Bridge Rd, Gainesville: 40,000-sq-ft beach, boat ramp, fishing pier, paved roads. The six Timberline glamping tents book separately. Winter 2026/27 reservations not yet released: the county may lay new water lines (county notice, per AWH 2026-10-11). --Claude

name: Cowan Lake State Park
note: Dam rehabilitation 2026-2028: the lake is drawn down 13.5 ft from November 1, 2026, construction early 2027 to spring 2028, water levels targeted to return summer 2028; fishing and kayaking at your own risk until the ramps can't be reached (ODNR, read 2026-10-30). --Claude
